candidate_table.name: Native deferred-tool / progressive discovery
candidate_table.operational_cost: no extra daemon; implementation lives in the host/API (defer_loading / search_tools)
candidate_table.solves_session_server_multiplication_not: MCP client best-practices document connecting a server only when needed and disconnecting afterwards; this is per-session lazy connect, not a shared process pool
candidate_table.when_daemon_dies: There is no shared gateway daemon. Ending the client session drops that session's tools only. Other sessions are unaffected.

candidate_table.name: Docker MCP Gateway
candidate_table.operational_cost: self-healing tax: Docker daemon + gateway process + container lifecycle; Desktop 4.59+ or DOCKER_MCP_IN_CONTAINER bypass
candidate_table.solves_lazy_tool_activation: partial: dynamic discovery from running servers; not equivalent to defer_loading (schemas of running servers still surface unless the client also defers)
candidate_table.solves_session_server_multiplication_not: yes on sse/streaming: one gateway can service multiple clients; servers are started on demand as containers
candidate_table.when_daemon_dies: docker mcp gateway run exiting drops the unified tool surface for every client attached to that gateway (stdio: one client; sse/streaming: all attached clients). Lazy-started server containers lose their supervisor; leftover containers are an orphan-tax, not a degraded client path.

candidate_table.name: IBM ContextForge MCP Gateway
candidate_table.operational_cost: self-healing tax: app replicas + PostgreSQL + Redis + (often) Nginx; Redis failure required an explicit degraded fallback
candidate_table.solves_lazy_tool_activation: partial: centralized discovery/registry; not client defer_loading
candidate_table.solves_session_server_multiplication_not: one HTTP/SSE/stdio wrapper endpoint federates many MCP/A2A/REST backends; multi-cluster Redis-backed federation is optional
candidate_table.when_daemon_dies: The federated endpoint is gone until the gateway (and its store) restart. Redis outage is a separate failure: PR 4074 added a circuit breaker and in-memory cache fallback, which is degraded mode for cache, not a replacement for the gateway process itself.

candidate_table.name: sparfenyuk/mcp-proxy
candidate_table.operational_cost: one extra process per bridge; no self-heal documented
candidate_table.solves_session_server_multiplication_not: transport switch, not a fleet multiplexer. named-server mode can expose several stdio servers under /servers/<name>/ but still spawns a stdio child per named server behind one proxy
candidate_table.when_daemon_dies: stdio-to-SSE client mode: that one session's bridge dies. SSE-to-stdio / named-server mode: the listen port dies and every client using it loses the spawned stdio child(ren).

candidate_table.name: supercorp-ai/supergateway
candidate_table.operational_cost: one extra npx/docker process per wrapped server
candidate_table.when_daemon_dies: The stdio-to-SSE/WS/HTTP listener dies; clients lose that one wrapped server. No multi-server federation.

claims.claim: The native baseline for lazy tool activation is client/API deferred loading (Anthropic defer_loading / tool-search, MCP progressive discovery with search_tools) plus list_changed, not a gateway daemon. The same MCP client guide also describes lazy server connect.
claims.strongest_caveat: Native lazy-server-connect is a host implementation pattern. A client that ignores the guide and eagerly spawns every stdio server still pays sessions x servers. That is a client defect, not a reason to federate gateways first.

claims.claim: Docker MCP Gateway is a persistent CLI/gateway process that unifies many containerized MCP servers, can serve multiple clients on sse/streaming, and lazy-starts a server container when a tool is needed.
claims.strongest_caveat: Lazy container start is still a daemon-supervised start. Docs do not show a client-side degraded path when the gateway process is dead.

claims.claim: ContextForge is a persistent registry/proxy that federates MCP/A2A/REST backends, optionally with Redis-backed multi-cluster federation. Its own Redis-outage work added circuit-breaker plus in-memory fallback, which is degraded-mode for a dependency, not proof that federation should be the first architecture.
claims.strongest_caveat: PR 4074's fallback covers Redis cache hangs, not a dead gateway replica or a lost Postgres. Multi-node session recovery remains a separate unfinished class in upstream issues.

claims.claim: mcp-proxy and supergateway are transport bridges (stdio <-> SSE/Streamable HTTP). They do not implement native deferred-tool activation. They add a process. named-server mode on mcp-proxy can front several stdio children but still spawns those children.
claims.strongest_caveat: A transport bridge can be a prerequisite for putting an HTTP gateway in front of a stdio-only server. That is an adapter cost, not a lazy-activation win over the native mechanism.

claims.claim: The recorded 05-ECO Tier-2 grade on gateway federation ('supervisor + degraded-mode fallback first') is CORROBORATED: every multiplexing candidate is a daemon with a self-healing tax; ContextForge had to add degraded Redis fallback; native deferred-tool already covers lazy activation without federation. No two-railed candidate beats the native mechanism on the lazy-activation axis.
claims.strongest_caveat: RES-0037 (live sessions x servers process count on this box) is absent. This corroboration is from public prior-art rails, not a local process-table measurement. A later local count could change the operational-cost magnitudes, not the daemon-liability polarity.
